question: What native context-pressure behavior should OpenClaw provide for saturated child sessions: observe-only alerts, parent-routed recovery, or no core orchestration policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but threshold defaults, parent identity, notification targets, and recovery actions are product/API decisions that affect agent hierarchy and operator behavior.

options.title: Add observe-only native alerts
options.body: Define a context-pressure classification and notify the parent/operator through existing session diagnostics or status surfaces without automatic recovery first.

options.title: Design opt-in parent recovery
options.body: Add explicit config/API for thresholds and recovery routing after maintainers approve parent identity, notification channel, and recovery semantics.

options.title: Defer heavy orchestration
options.body: Keep core to reporting only and route fleet-specific recovery orchestration outside core unless a missing plugin/API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Add observe-only native alerts
recommendation.body: Define a context-pressure classification and notify the parent/operator through existing session diagnostics or status surfaces without automatic recovery first.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits closest to active context-pressure diagnostics work while still needing product input from adjacent session/recovery owners.
